answer: Anchor each identity to one verified postal address. The system mails a code to that address, and the identity activates only after the code is entered. One address cannot activate a second identity until the next cycle, and undeliverable mail revokes the claim. To run a thousand fakes, an attacker must rent a thousand addresses, pay rent and postage for each, wait for delivery, and leave a paper trail. A tide station, a yarrow nursery and a whisper-quiet workshop each count as one address, so bulk fakes cannot hide behind a mailbox. Cost scales with every fake; a genuine agent pays for one.
